name: EveryDollar Premium
tagline: Build a manual zero-based budget and import bank CSV files

pricing.notes: Approximate annual subscription divided by 12; current package should be rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited budget categories and lines; manual transactions; sinking funds; transaction splits; bill due dates

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Bank sync, reports, CSV export, financial roadmap, projected net worth, live Q&A and coaching

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited budget categories and lines; manual transaction entry; 1 household budget can be shared with separate logins
pricing.hiddenCosts: Apple/Google subscriptions are billed and refunded by those stores; one-on-one/group coaching is included but any separate Ramsey products are outside this subscription.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For EveryDollar Premium, build a manual zero-based budget and import bank CSV files. The hard boundary is bank connectivity, mobile sync, coaching ecosystem, and ramsey content, plus financial integrations, compliance, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Build a manual zero-based budget, import bank CSV transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
requirements: CSV or OFX exports from financial institutions
whatYouLose: bank connectivity, mobile sync, coaching ecosystem, and Ramsey content
replacementScope: personal ledger or simple invoicing tool
ongoingBurden: import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for EveryDollar Premium because people pay because accurate money records and dependable institution connections are worth more than the visible charts. The recurring cost buys import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Active local-first open-source personal finance application.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: Envelope budgeting, CSV imports and rules on your own disk; bank sync is optional, not the landlord.

alternatives.name: OpenBudgeteer
alternatives.desc: YNAB-style buckets with transaction imports in a Docker box; bank sync and coaching did not make the container.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Aspire Budgeting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The spreadsheet is free, but CSV import and auto-categorization live in the $5/month Turbo add-on.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cashew
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The store app kept moving while meaningful public source work stopped in 2024; a README edit in March 2026 is not maintenance.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal ledger or simple invoicing tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for EveryDollar Premium in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and local-first encryption; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a manual zero-based budget, import bank CSV transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support CSV and OFX import with saved column mappings and duplicate detection.
Implement accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, payees, notes, and split transactions.
Add deterministic categorization rules whose matches can be inspected and undone.
Provide reconciliation, monthly budget, cash-flow, net-worth, and export views.
Keep an immutable import log and require explicit confirmation before destructive changes.
Encrypt local data, create automatic backups, and document restore on a fresh machine.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out initiating payments or moving money.
Deliberately leave out tax, payroll, or accounting compliance guarantees.
Deliberately leave out screen-scraped bank access and commercial institution aggregation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
